analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one failure-mode table row near line 2316. The row documents that an unexpired Autopilot placement hold excludes a slot from eviction and gives its weights no free_for_load_gb reclaim credit. No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, cache encryption or authorization logic is modified. The two supplied units (lines 802-1609) are unchanged base context covering GLM media, calibration, deadlines and MTP, and they carry no diff hunks. I found no regression against the threat model, including TB-007, T-041, T-029 or the prefix-cache and attestation entries. The only security-adjacent point is the documented behavior itself. Autopilot holds can block eviction and cold loads, a possible availability or resource-pinning concern (cf. T-029 monopolising provider resources). The hold's bounding (expiry), its source and its authorization are in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Autopilot/ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift, which is not supplied. I therefore cannot judge whether a hold can be abused by a coordinator or consumer, and I report no finding. Integration should check that code if Autopilot placements are otherwise changed in this PR: the hold expiry is bounded, only authenticated coordinator-originated placements can create holds, and held weights cannot starve loads indefinitely.
